# Game Modes
Some game modes add to or change the Honor Code.
## Insurgency The Yautja have no knowledge of the insurgency or unrest within the colony at round start, so the colony is not considered a worthy hunting ground.
- Yautja must wait 30 minutes before going down to the colony. - Until the Yautja have witnessed direct conflict in the colony between INSFOR and GOVFOR, there should be no hunting of prey except in very special circumstances. For example, a Yautja who witnesses a serial killer antagonist murder several colonists may consider them worthy prey. - Yautja should never side with or make any kind of agreement with GOVFOR or INSFOR, except for a temporary truce to deal with abominations or aberrations. - Directly interacting with colonists, or otherwise causing unrest by not concealing your presence in the colony, may lead to in-character punishment. Examples are running through the colony cloaked and bumping into people, or showing yourself to several people uncloaked. It may be escalated to removal of your whitelist should it become a recurring issue. Once direct conflict between INSFOR and GOVFOR begins, this no longer applies. - Any colonist the Yautja directly observe being involved in combat is from then on considered worthy prey, but the Yautja must make sure the colonist can put up an adequate fight at the time of the confrontation. - Yautja may never willingly let themselves be infected by a rider, and must self-destruct if infected involuntarily. - Hunting during Insurgency should be taken slower, with emphasis on stalking prey for an extended time, because of how easily it can impact the round.
## Yautja purges Should the Yautja witness We-Yu experimenting with xenomorphs, they may purge the facility to safeguard their hunting ground. All xenomorphs are considered worthy prey during the purge.
- Yautja have no round start knowledge of the facility, and cannot infiltrate it to bait a purge. The xenomorphs must be released into the colony or left in view outside the facility. This includes Greenos. - Wendigos are not a valid reason to start a purge. Wendigos are considered worthy prey once they leave the facility. - Yautja may not start hunts inside the facility, unless pursuing a fleeing Wendigo or other worthy prey. - If GOVFOR aligns itself with We-Yu and deploys to assist before the purge is complete, the Yautja must abandon the purge to minimize collateral damage to GOVFOR assets. - The purge is led by the highest-ranking Yautja on the hunt. If Yautja of equal rank cannot decide who leads, they may duel for the honor.
## Force on Force Yautja should never side with or make any kind of agreement with GOVFOR or OPFOR, except for a temporary truce to deal with abominations or aberrations.
